data.name: Bheravi
data.long_meaning: Bheravi is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Bhara’, meaning strength or power. In Hindu mythology, Bheravi is an epithet of the goddess Durga, representing fearlessness and courage. This name is ideal for parents who wish to bestow their daughter with the qualities of bravery and strength.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bheravi holds a significant place in Hindu culture, especially as an epithet for the goddess Durga. Durga is a form of the divine mother, an embodiment of feminine power and strength. She is the protector of all beings and the slayer of various demons that threaten the peace and harmony of the universe. The name Bheravi reminds us of this fearless and powerful aspect of the goddess and encourages the qualities of courage, strength, and fearlessness. Through this name, the cultural heritage of India's rich mythology and traditions continues to inspire and influence us.
data.spiritual_significance: Bheravi is not only a beautiful name but also carries deep spiritual significance. The name is a reminder of the inner strength and courage that resides in every individual. It encourages us to tap into our inner resources, cultivate inner peace, and overcome our fears. Durga, as Bheravi, represents the fearless aspect of the divine which resonates with the fearless aspect of the human spirit. By invoking the blessings of this divine figure, we are encouraged to develop the qualities of courage, strength, and fearlessness in our everyday lives. ultimately, the name Bheravi serves as a constant reminder of the inner strength, courage, and divine protection that we all possess within us.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bheravi mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. The name Bheravi carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Bheravi was a charioteer of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty. During the Kurukshetra war, Bheravi was instrumental in the defeat of Arjuna, one of the Pandava brothers. Later, Bheravi showed mercy to Arjuna and helped him perform the last rites of Bhishma.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bheravi, a goddess worshipped in the chanting of the Bheragita hymns of the Jain faith. The name Bheravi carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Bheravi is considered a goddess of prosperity and fertility. She is revered in the Jain community for her role in the story of Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara. Bheravi is believed to have appeared before Mahavira to offer her protection and guide him on his spiritual journey.

Lastly, on Etsy and other handmade marketplaces, various spiritual fashion accessories, such as jewelry and clothing, are named after 'Bheravi' and feature intricate Hindu motifs and symbolism.
